'''Anders Olof Gunnar Källén''' (13 February 1926 – 13 October 1968) was a Swedish [[theoretical physicist]] and professor at [[Lund University]], known for his work on [[Correlation function (quantum field theory)|correlation functions]] in [[quantum field theory]]. He died at the age of 42 as a result of a plane crash.

==Biography==
Anders Olof Gunnar Källén was born in 1926 in [[Kristianstad]], Sweden.<ref name=":1">{{Citation |last=Jarlskog |first=Cecilia |chapter=Bengt Källén: The Childhood and Youth of Gunnar Källén |date=2014 |title=Portrait of Gunnar Källén |pages=3–10 |editor-last=Jarlskog |editor-first=Cecilia |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-319-00627-7_1 |access-date=2024-04-23 |place=Cham |publisher=Springer International Publishing |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-00627-7_1 |isbn=978-3-319-00626-0|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> His father, Yngve Källén, was a teacher of physics and mathematics, and together they published a paper on the theory of relativity.<ref name=":1" /> Gunnar's brother was the embryologist {{Ill|Bengt Källén|sv}}.<ref name=":1" />

Källén earned his doctorate at Lund in 1950 working with [[Torsten Gustafson]], who was in close correspondence with [[Wolfgang Pauli]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Källén |first=Gunnar |title=Formal integration of the equations of quantum theory in the Heisenberg representation |date=1950 |publisher=Lund University |id=https://libris.kb.se/bib/1418312}}</ref> He worked at [[CERN]]'s theoretical division from 1952 to 1957,<ref>{{cite book|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-00627-7_6 | title=Portrait of Gunnar Källén | year=2013 | pages=25–28 | last1 = Jarlskog | first1 = Cecilia| chapter=As a Staff Member of the Newborn CERN | isbn=978-3-319-00626-0 }}</ref> which, at that time, was situated at the Institute for Theoretical Physics of the University of Copenhagen, later to be named the [[Niels Bohr Institute]].<ref>[http://timeline.web.cern.ch/closure-of-cern’s-theoretical-study-division-in-copenhagen "Closure of CERN’s Theoretical Study Division in Copenhagen"]</ref> Afterwards he worked at [[Nordic Institute for Theoretical Physics|Nordita]] from 1957 to 1958, and then began a professorship at Lund University.

Källén's research focused on [[quantum field theory]] and [[elementary particle]] physics. His developments included the so-called [[Källén–Lehmann spectral representation]] of [[Correlation function (quantum field theory)|correlation functions]] in quantum field theory, and he made contributions to [[quantum electrodynamics]], especially in renormalization. He also worked with the axiomatic formulation of quantum field theory, which led to contributions to the theory of functions of several complex variables, and collaborated on the Pauli–Källén equation.

The [[Källén function]], as well as the Källén–Yang–Feldman formalism and the Källén–Sabry potentials are named after him.

=== Plane crash ===
Källén was an avid pilot, who, having been fascinated by flying since childhood, started taking lessons in 1964.<ref name=":0" /> He was flying a [[Piper PA-28 Cherokee]] Arrow from [[Malmö]] to CERN when his plane crashed during an [[emergency landing]] in [[Hanover]], Germany in 1968.<ref name=":0">{{cite book|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-00627-7_31 | title=Portrait of Gunnar Källén | year=2013 | pages=135–140 | last1 = Jarlskog | first1 = Cecilia| chapter=Erland Källén: My Father's Passion for Flying and His Mortal Accident | isbn=978-3-319-00626-0 }}</ref> His two passengers, one of them his wife, survived the crash.

Many years after his death, [[Cecilia Jarlskog]] edited the book ''Portrait of Gunnar Källén: A Physics Shooting Star and Poet of Early Quantum Field Theory'' (Springer, 2013) with nine invited contributors, all of whom had a personal acquaintance with Källén.<ref>{{cite book|chapter=Invited Contributors |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=W4u4BAAAQBAJ&pg=PR25 | page=xxv |title=Portrait of Gunnar Källén: A Physics Shooting Star and Poet of Early Quantum Field Theory | isbn=9783319006277 | editor=Jarlskog, Cecilia | date=21 October 2013 |publisher=Springer}}</ref> The book consists mainly of testimonies by Källén's colleagues.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Martin, André|url=https://cerncourier.com/a/portrait-of-gunnar-kallen-a-physics-shooting-star-and-poet-of-early-quantum-field-theory/|title=Review of ''Portrait of Gunnar Källén: A Physics Shooting Star and Poet of Early Quantum Field Theory'' edited by Cecilia Jarlskog |journal=CERN Courier |date=23 September 2014 }}</ref> [[Steven Weinberg]], whose first published physics paper was motivated by Källén, wrote one of the book's chapters. The chapter deals with Källén's research and is the written version of a 2009 lecture by Weinberg.<ref>{{cite book|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-00627-7_61|chapter=Steven Weinberg: Living with Infinities |title=Portrait of Gunnar Källén |year=2014 |editor=Jarlskog, Cecilia |pages=279–292 |isbn=978-3-319-00626-0 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Weinberg "Living with infinities" - Källén Lecture 2009|date=January 14, 2022|publisher=Andrea Idini|website=YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rFd9PIy_zXs}} (lecture recorded on February 13, 2009)</ref>
